clause_i.reason: An observation-free route can be fixed from the exact level-1 geometry: hold morph-taller for seven 40 ms physics ticks to reach h=101, release, then hold slide-right until terminal. With no layout key the generator uses the linear branch; gap=0 replaces the floor with a full-width floor, and all seal centers are to the right of the initial x=100 (the random ranges are approximately x=130-160, 270-325, 405-475, and 835-865). The h=101 parcel fits beneath the clearance-105 shelf and its top is within 10 units of the y=310 seal, so the fixed rightward sweep succeeds without recent-frame information. Under the primary pass/fail outcome, this supplies an observation-free success-maximizing q; the random offsets do not require a different route.

clause_ii.reason: A bounded-window mapping can ignore its input window and follow the same fixed action schedule. The configured 80 ms window and three chronological frames are therefore sufficient but unnecessary for selecting a success-maximizing action in this configuration.

clause_iii.reason: The only non-clock change during a no-new-action interval is finite inertial coasting plus floor-supported physics. At difficulty 1 there is no unsupported gap and no alcove; seals remain visible and collectible, horizontal motion is reversible, and height can be corrected while the parcel remains supported. Waiting can move the parcel, but it does not make a required control opportunity unavailable or strictly reduce eventual verifier success; a max_ticks deadline is not a qualifying cause under the definition. Thus no Delta and grouped mode has the required strict Q loss from a common visible process.

common_visible_process: No qualifying common process exists. The visible parcel coasts under inertia, but in the exact linear full-floor level-1 room that motion does not close or degrade an outcome-affecting opportunity; a fixed rightward sweep remains available after any such delay.

pre_run.reason: All generated level-1 instances have the same linear full-floor topology and only bounded horizontal seal offsets. A fixed preparation raises h from 80 to 101, then a final continuous right hold starts the autonomous outcome interval; no further outcome-affecting input is needed before the sweep reaches every seal and the task becomes solved. The source structure therefore implies at least half (in fact all) generated seeds admit a pre-run solution; no percentage is claimed. A 100-seed replay probe corroborated this result.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 1 is very_easy with clearance 105, gap 0, reach 100, alcove 0, drag 0.65; full interaction is implemented and the configured observation is 80 ms with three frames.

The supplied difficulty parameters are used directly; because level 1 has no layout key, generation takes the linear branch, gap 0 creates a full-width floor, alcove 0 adds no well, and the seal coordinates vary only within fixed horizontal ranges.
The parcel has fixed area, explicit height bounds, four physics substeps per tick, inertial horizontal velocity with drag, gravity/floor collision, monotone seal collection, and terminal checks.

Full mode renders body-arrow controls and hides the simplified console; task time advances from performance.now at tick_ms, and pointer holds/releases set the control while the animation frame loop advances the simulation.
The visible body-control overlay is positioned over the parcel, while the alternate console is hidden when the full interface is selected.
The authoritative replay applies the same physics, enforces the selected full input surface and release-before-new-hold rule, and passes only when replay reaches solved with every seal collected.
Verification loads the exported result and invokes the independent Concertina Courier replay grader rather than trusting client collection claims.

The reference solver uses state feedback and short prediction for harder routes, and its task-time waiting is delegated to the harness; this private solver is wiring evidence, not policy-visible information.
